title: No source gives the ledger's access shape: the element names inside the actions payload beyond the legacy list, the grant, incident and review-due elements of the decision-log read, the use of the access code AC-VERS, and the catalogue entry format of MSG-P7-009
source: Legacy RWB-E1-039 sections 7, 8, 11, 12, 14 and 18 against FSD P7 v3 A2.1 to A2.5, TSD P7 v2, the Ownership Map decision-log rows of P7, the context pack of P7, and Architecture v5 slides 13, 28 and 42
description: The legacy story fixes the facts of an access entry and none of the shapes the split needs. Section 11 names the fields of decision_log_entry and section 12 names the request and response of the access log and of the grant, but the actions element is described only by words: area, right, field IDs with the masking position, filter, row count, document ID, grant ID, incident reference and reason code, with no element names and no nesting. The decision-log read of the target is declared by API-P7-006 and API-P7-007 of the TSD, whose answer carries no grant, no incident and no review due element, so the three elements this slice answers for the review of a break-glass use exist only as names chosen here. The code AC-VERS sits in LOV-DECISION of the legacy preconditions and is used by no criterion, no rule and no flow of the legacy story, the FSD P7 or the TSD P7, so what it records is not fixed anywhere. Finally the message identifiers MSG-P7-003, MSG-P7-009 and MSG-P4-002 are fixed by the legacy story but their catalogue entry format is not, and the parameter path of the parameters contract is named by no document.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-039 section 11 (DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018, DF-DEC-002, DF-DEC-003, DF-DEC-014, DF-DEC-016, DF-DEC-030), section 12 (the BreakGlassActivation and AccessLogEntry shapes and the published interface AccessEventPublisher), section 14 (MSG-P7-003, MSG-P7-009, MSG-P4-002), section 18; FSD P7 v3 A2.1.4, A2.2.4 and A2.5.4, which carry no access criterion and no access field list; the Ownership Map rows of P7 (decision_log_entry; GET /decision-log; GET /decision-log/{entryId}); context pack P7 (service, naming and shared platform rules); Architecture v5 slides 13, 28 and 42
proposed: Keep the legacy list as the minimum content of actions, name the three read elements grantId, incidentReference and reviewDueAt as working names until the contract baseline of the service publishes them, accept AC-VERS as an access code and map it like the other five without fixing its subject, keep the legacy message identifiers with the published catalogue format to come from the message catalogue owner, and take the parameter path from the parameters contract of rwb-case.
